market_context: United States; commercially washed shell eggs sold under refrigeration
title: Should eggs be refrigerated?

seo.title: Should eggs be refrigerated? U.S. egg storage explained
seo.meta_description: Yes. In the U.S., commercially sold shell eggs should stay refrigerated at 40°F (4°C) or below because they are washed and sold under a cold chain.
seo.search_intent: Understand why U.S. eggs need refrigeration, how to store them, and why advice differs from some European countries.

excerpt: Yes. In the United States, commercially sold shell eggs should be refrigerated promptly at 40°F (4°C) or below and kept cold until use. U.S. eggs are commercially washed and normally sold under refrigeration, so storing them on the counter after purchase breaks that cold chain. Keep the carton on an interior refrigerator shelf and take out only the eggs you are about to use.
content_html:
In a U.S. grocery store, eggs are normally sold from a refrigerated case, and that cold case is part of the food-safety system rather than a merchandising choice. Commercial shell eggs bought in the United States should be kept at 40°F (4°C) or below after purchase.

The advice can seem odd if you have seen eggs sitting on unrefrigerated shelves in Europe. The difference is largely about processing and temperature management, not about eggs behaving differently on opposite sides of the Atlantic.

U.S. eggs are washed and then kept cold

Commercial processing in the United States includes washing and sanitizing shell eggs. That helps remove surface contamination, but it also alters the shell's natural protective coating. Refrigeration then becomes an important part of limiting bacterial growth.

FDA guidance therefore tells consumers to buy eggs from a refrigerated case and put them promptly into a refrigerator at 40°F or below.

Once they are refrigerated, keep the temperature steady

A cold egg should not spend hours warming on the counter and then go back into the refrigerator. Warming can create condensation on the shell, while extended time at room temperature gives bacteria more opportunity to multiply.

FDA's general rule for refrigerated perishables is no more than two hours at room temperature, shortened to one hour when the air temperature is above 90°F (32°C).

An interior shelf is better than the refrigerator door

The door warms slightly every time it opens. An interior shelf stays more consistent. Keeping eggs in the original carton also protects them from breakage and strong odors and keeps the date information with the eggs.

A refrigerator thermometer can be useful because the appliance dial does not always show the actual food temperature.

How long do raw shell eggs keep in the refrigerator?

FDA recommends using shell eggs within about three weeks for best quality. Other U.S. storage charts may show somewhat longer refrigerated windows, but the carton date and how the eggs have been handled still matter.

Even under refrigeration, quality changes with age: the air cell grows, the white becomes thinner and the yolk membrane weakens.

There is no reason to wash commercial eggs again at home

Commercial eggs have already been washed before sale. Washing them again in the sink is unnecessary and can splash microorganisms onto nearby surfaces.

Eggs with cracked shells should generally be discarded unless the crack happened during your own handling and the contents are immediately transferred to a clean container and cooked thoroughly.

Why can European stores look different?

Many European systems do not wash Grade A table eggs before retail and instead emphasize avoiding temperature fluctuations and condensation before sale. That is why eggs may be displayed on unrefrigerated shelves there.

It does not mean refrigerated U.S. eggs can safely be switched to the same storage routine after purchase. Follow the cold-chain system under which the eggs were produced and sold.

The practical rule

For eggs bought in the United States: buy them cold, take them home promptly, refrigerate at 40°F or below and keep them cold until you are ready to use them.

The store refrigerator and your home refrigerator are two parts of one continuous cold chain.

faq.question: Can U.S. eggs be left on the counter?
faq.answer: Commercially refrigerated eggs should not be stored on the counter. FDA's general two-hour limit for refrigerated perishables applies, shortened to one hour above 90°F.

faq.question: Where should eggs go in the refrigerator?
faq.answer: Keep them in their original carton on an interior shelf where temperature is more stable than in the door.

faq.question: Why are eggs not refrigerated in some European stores?
faq.answer: Processing and temperature-management systems differ. Many European table eggs are not washed before retail and are kept at a relatively constant temperature to avoid condensation.
